column1: # golden_bands.tsv -- the ONE table that says how wide a golden row's band is,
# by WHAT KIND OF NUMBER the row holds (C384, 2026-11-13).  Read by
# bin/curate/golden_bands.py (the recorder's band writer, the cross-platform
# transformation and the rewrite tool) and by bin/curate/check_golden_bands.py.
# A GOLDEN IS TWO CLAIMS.  On the platform that recorded it: "this has not
# moved" -- the band written in the file, tight.  Elsewhere: "this reproduces as
# well as this kind of number can" -- the file passed through THIS table, in a
# temporary file, never written to the tree (golden_bands.py cross; bin/runTests
# does it when the running platform is not the recording one).  So the classes
# fall in two GROUPS:
#   platform  (count, condition, parameter, objective): NEVER on disk.  Applied
#             only in cross mode, and never tighter than the file's own band.
#   residual  (residual_*): ON DISK as `abs:<v>`, because a closure residual is
#             round-off of a balance and its meaning is absolute on any platform.
# A row of NO class is a DIRECT RESULT: the band of the file, in every mode.
# Columns (TAB separated):  class | kinds | name regex | key regex | rule | param | reason
#   kinds       comma list of golden kinds the class applies to
#   name regex  matched (fullmatch) against the row's name column; `.*` = any
#   key regex   matched (fullmatch) against the row's key column
#   rule        rel  -- a relative band, `param` is the number
#               abs_frac_of_term -- an ABSOLUTE band `abs:<param x term>`, the
#                   term named by golden_bands.py (boundary_denominator |
#                   unit Q_kW | ledger terms)
#               abs -- (C429) a FIXED absolute band `abs:max(param, 1e-4 x |expected|)`
#                   on every NON-ZERO row of the class (an expected 0 keeps the absolute band it was authored with): a residual or closure is round-off,
#                   and a relative band on it is meaningless.  ON DISK, any platform.
#               abs_if_tiny -- (C429) as abs with band `param`, but ONLY on a row whose
#                   expected value is non-zero and at most 1e-9 in magnitude (a quantity that is zero
#                   by construction and prints round-off); other rows keep their band.
#   Floor: an absolute band is never written below 1e-9 in the row's own unit
#   (the residual_charge band, 1e-12, is the one declared exception: its own gate's TOL).
#   Groups by name: residual_* and zero_* are written on disk as `abs:<v>`.
#   C429: a NON-ZERO expected value is compared RELATIVELY whatever its size (bin/runTests
#   within_tol); only an `abs` class, an `abs:` row or an exactly-zero expected is absolute.
# The first matching line wins.  Anchor rows and `exact` rows are never touched.
count
column7: A count of iterations or evaluations is decided by comparisons of 1e-6 on a max-norm objective (FitObjective.cpp minimise: restart ends when the best value improved by less than 1e-6 relative), so it is chaotic in the last digits: measured 2265 of 4174 minimax_evaluations rows differ between two platforms, max 1.43 from 5 restart passes against 2.  The row asserts "within a factor of three" and still fails a solver that needs ten times more.

column1: condition
column7: The condition number of J^T J in a flat valley moves with the last digits of the parameters: measured median 2.3e-3, p95 0.22, max 1.4e3 between two platforms.  Rows still red are pinned findings (platform_divergence_debt.tsv).

column1: parameter
column7: A fitted parameter is defined to about sqrt of the least-squares tolerance (FitParameters.cpp:662, tolerance 1e-4 on the relative change of chi2) in the flat directions of J^T J; measured p95 0.19 and max 0.35.  Five times that square root; rows still red are findings.

column1: objective
column7: A statistic of an optimiser's answer inherits its stopping tolerance (least squares 1e-4 on the change of chi2): a hundred times that.  Measured median 1.2e-3, p95 0.09, max 0.39; rows still red are flat-valley findings, not a wider class.

column1: residual_boundary
column7: A closure residual is round-off of a balance, so it is compared on an ABSOLUTE band written in the row: 1e-5 of the energy the plant exchanges (`residual_denom_kW` of the same result block; measured platform difference at most 6.4e-7 of it).  With no published denominator: abs:max(1e-3 kW, 1e-4 x |expected|) -- the 1e-3 kW floor, never tighter than the relative 1e-4 the row always had (flash20 differs by 4.3e-3 kW of 42.86 between two runs on one platform).

column1: residual_hx
column7: The gap is the unit's own enthalpy closure in the unit of its duty: 1e-8 of that unit's |Q_kW| (measured 1e-10).

column1: residual_ledger
column7: The campaign and dynamic energy ledgers: 1e-9 of the largest pinned energy term of that ledger (measured 6e-13 and 2e-15).

column1: residual_closure
column7: A mass, element, solute or energy closure FRACTION is round-off of a balance: the row is compared on an absolute band of 1e-9, the bound the engine itself refuses a per-solute closure above (check_mass_closure.py:122, "refused above 1e-9") and the floor of this table (golden_bands.py FLOOR).  Never tighter than the 1e-4 relative band the row used to carry (band = max(1e-9, 1e-4 x |expected|)), so a closure that really is 1e-5 keeps its old width.  The conservation gates hold the real tolerances (check_campaign_closure.py:86 CAMPAIGN_TOL 1e-3, check_mass_closure BAND): this class only says that round-off moving between 1e-16 and 1e-12 is not a change.

column1: residual_mass_abs
column7: The absolute mass imbalance of a plant [kg per the row's own basis] is round-off of the same balance (census 2026-11-18: 65 rows, 7e-19 to 3.5e-10): the 1e-9 floor, max(1e-9, 1e-4 x |expected|).

column1: residual_charge
column7: Electroneutrality residual |sum z m| / sum |z| m of a speciation: round-off on a sum of ~1e-2 molalities, held to 1e-12 by check_charge_balance.py:44 (TOL = 1.0e-12); census 126 rows, 2e-18 to 4.4e-13.  max(1e-12, 1e-4 x |expected|).

column1: residual_pore
column7: The DSPM-DE pore's own numerics (PoreTransportBench.H:110-113): the station Newton's final residual (held to 1e-12 by the bench default, PoreNernstPlanck.H:325, and 1e-9 in the module, SpiralWoundModule.cpp:2057) and the closure checks measured on the answer (electroneutrality, zero current, flux constancy, permeate charge), all dimensionless round-off of the solved pore; census 200 rows, 1e-18 to 1.6e-13.  max(1e-9, 1e-4 x |expected|).

column1: residual_newton
column7: A Newton residual is the norm the solver stopped at: held to the NewtonND tolerance 1e-8 (NewtonND.H:182); the reactors and the pellet stop far below it (census 2e-18 to 3e-13).  A value above 1e-8 is non-convergence, not drift.  max(1e-8, 1e-4 x |expected|).

column1: residual_identity
column7: A verification deviation that asserts an identity (the enthalpy surface against its own Kirchhoff and Cp integrals, HConsistency.H; the rated-permeate gap; the ENRTL reduction pin; a friction correlation against its published anchor; the isotherm's twin-evaluation gate; the entropy ledger's ideal-gas gap; the frequency-response fit residual of an exact response; the fixed bed's telescopic `mass_closure_<species>` identities, which check_campaign_closure.py names as discretisation identities and not physical closures): numerical-differentiation or round-off noise, measured 1e-16 to 2.2e-10 on the census; 1e-8 is fifty times the largest and a wrong Cp term moves these rows by 1e-3 or more.  max(1e-8, 1e-4 x |expected|).

column1: residual_saturation
column7: A saturation index at an EQUILIBRIUM is zero to the speciation solver's own admission threshold: a mineral is admitted at SI > 1e-10 and evicted at amount < -1e-10 (SpeciationSolver.cpp:2178, :2156), so an index of 1e-12 to 1e-10 printed for a phase at equilibrium is the solver's residual (census: pb82 calcite 3.2e-11, brackish feed 5.8e-12).  An SI of real size (0.3, -1.2) keeps its 1e-4 relative band through max(1e-9, 1e-4 x |expected|); only an index within the solver's tolerance of zero is judged absolutely.

column1: zero_balance
column7: The size of an ASSUMPTION that is zero when nothing is fabricated (check_campaign_closure.py names carrier_makeup_rel "the SIZE of an assumption, not a closure"): when the bed fabricates no carrier the row prints the round-off of the carrier balance (census 1e-15 to 2.5e-11), and batch24_blowdown_inert showed it is not even reproducible in sign.  A row recorded at round-off is compared absolutely at 1e-9 (the closure floor); a real fabricated amount keeps its relative band.

column1: zero_pressure_drop
column7: A pressure difference of two cells of an isobaric inert blowdown prints the round-off of a pressure sum (1.5e-11 Pa, sign not reproducible); a row recorded at round-off is compared absolutely at 1e-6 Pa (a micropascal against a bed at 1e5 Pa is 1e-11 relative, below the pressure's own convergence).  A real pressure drop keeps its relative band.

column1: zero_duty
column7: A duty or a boundary/closure remainder that is zero by construction (an adiabatic bed, a balanced plant) prints round-off of the enthalpy sums (census 1e-13 to 2e-10 kW): a row whose expected value is at most 1e-9 is compared as the exact-zero row always was, absolutely, at UNIT_TOL_KW = 1e-4 kW (check_energy_closure.py:788).  A duty of any real size keeps its relative band: the class touches only a row recorded at round-off.

column1: direct
column7: A direct result of the run (a flash duty, a stream flow, a KPI of a unit, a word): the band of the golden file in every mode, 1e-4 unless the case authored another.  It exists so that EVERY row of every golden has a class (check_golden_bands).
